column2: Retain Aaron's divisions and the four names Nadab, Abioud, Eleazar and Ithamar. Abioud is the selected name form and is not normalized to Abihu.
Retain the first two dying before their father without sons and the surviving two serving as priests. Before can concern his presence or lifetime; no cause of death is added here.
Retain David with Sadok of Eleazar and Achimelech of Ithamar, and the repeated inspection, ministry and ancestral-house criteria. The two priestly family affiliations remain distinct.
Retain Eleazar's greater number of leaders, sixteen houses for his line and eight for Ithamar's. The selected ruler-of-mighty-men description is not silently reduced to a simple total of priests.
Retain allotment alongside one another and both rulers of holy things and rulers of the Lord in both families. Do not replace these two titles with an inferred one-family-per-office arrangement.
column3: The institutional meaning of the two ruler expressions remains unresolved.

column2: Retain Samaias son of Nathanael recording, all named participants and one house at a time for each family. No two-from-Eleazar-to-one-from-Ithamar ratio is imposed to reconcile the totals.
column3: The Greek case shifts in the participant list and the one-one allotment formula require syntactic review; with is an inherited connective supply.

column2: Retain Jarib first and Ideia second. Their order is an outcome of the lot, not an assertion of ancestral seniority.
Retain Charem third and Seorim fourth. Both ordinals continue the lot sequence begun in verse 7.
Retain Melchia fifth and Miamin sixth, without normalizing either name from another priestly roster.
Retain Kos seventh and Abia eighth. The selected Kos form is not expanded with an unexpressed initial element.
Retain Jesus ninth and Sechenia tenth. Jesus is the inherited rendering of this priestly name; no identification with a New Testament person is implied.
Retain Eliasib eleventh and Jakim twelfth. The two adjacent ranks remain separate allotments.
Retain Ochchopha thirteenth and Isbaal fourteenth. Neither unusual name is silently harmonized with another textual tradition.
Retain Belga fifteenth and Emmer sixteenth, continuing the explicit sequence without reordering by family.
Retain Chezir seventeenth and Aphesse eighteenth. The spelling choices remain provisional onomastic decisions.
Retain Phetaia nineteenth and Ezekiel twentieth. The latter is a list name, not an added identification with the prophet.
Retain Jachin twenty-first and Gamoul twenty-second. Both selected ordinals are explicitly represented.
Retain Dalaia twenty-third and Maasai twenty-fourth. The list ends at twenty-four without adding a separate summary unit.

Retain inspection, ministry, entering the house, ordinance through Aaron their father and the Lord's command. Father denotes the ancestral priestly relation, not immediate paternity of every listed man.
Retain the remaining Levites, Ambram to Soubael and Soubael to Jadia. The repeated sons headings preserve the two generations.
Retain Jesias as ruler for Raabia. No missing sons heading is reconstructed as an additional group.
Retain the Issari designation, Salomoth and his sons' Jath. The selected Issari form is not silently replaced by the earlier Issaar spelling.
Retain sons of Jediou followed by Amadia second, Jaziel third and Jokom fourth. Do not insert Hebron or an unnamed first ruler to repair the selected genealogy.
column3: The relation of Jediou to the prior Idoud and the absent first rank remains an open textual and genealogical question.

column2: Retain Oziel's Micha and Micha's Samer. The second sons heading marks another generation rather than another brother of Micha.
Retain Isia as Micha's brother and Zacharia among Isia's sons. The explicit brother relation is not replaced by a father-son chain.
Retain Merari's Mooli and Mousi followed by the separate Ozia's sons and Bonni's sons fragments. No connecting descent or missing personal name is invented.
column3: The relation of Ozia and Bonni to the preceding family is unresolved; the semicolons disclose rather than repair the fragmentary list.

column2: Retain the Merari/Ozia construction and Isoam, Zakchour and Abdi. The repeated sons expression remains despite the difficult attachment.
column3: Which clause his sons resumes requires specialist genealogical review; no conventional Jahaziah/Beno reconstruction is substituted.

column2: Retain Mooli's Eleazar and Ithamar, then Eleazar dying without sons. Do not substitute Kis for the selected Ithamar to align chapter 23.
Retain the repeated Kis and the single Iramael under plural sons. No additional sibling or connecting genealogy is supplied.
Retain Mousi's Mooli, Eder and Jarimoth and the conclusion identifying Levite ancestral houses. The repeated names match this local list without proving identities across all genealogies.

Retain lot participation like Aaron's sons, the named witnesses, ancestral heads, araab and singular his younger brethren. The opaque form and number mismatch are not silently replaced with eldest and youngest.
column3: Araab remains untranslated and unapproved; its function and the antecedent of his require lexical and witness review.

column2: Retain David and the military rulers appointing Asaph's, Aiman's and Idithon's sons, instrumental utterance and head-by-head numbering. Inspired words is a contextual interpretation of the utterance verb, supported by the subsequent prophet designation, not an explicit separate inspiration adjective.
column3: Kinyrai and nablai remain inherited borrowed instrument names here; consistency with harps and lyres elsewhere requires lexical review.

column2: Retain Zakchour, Joseph, Nathanias and Erael, repeated sons of Asaph and both attachment phrases. Asaph is explicitly called prophet; the second attachment to the king does not turn the king into that prophet.
Retain all six named sons including Semei, their father Idithon, the kinyra and both thanksgiving and praise. Do not omit Semei to produce a five-name list from another witness.
Retain all fourteen names in the selected order, including separate Ananias and Anani and the joined Romemthi-od. Name phrases are not reinterpreted as a continuous lyric here.

Retain Aiman playing for the king in God's words, raising a horn and the exact fourteen sons and three daughters. No royal seer title is imported where this selected clause uses the playing expression.
column3: The horn's referent and whether its raising belongs to musical action, divine exaltation or another relation remain unresolved.

column2: Retain the father with the hymn-singers, the three instrument categories and the king followed by Asaph, Idithon and Aiman. Under is an inherited administrative interpretation of the attachment expression.
column3: The grammatical reach of the attachment phrase and its unusual agreement need syntactic review.

column2: Retain the total 288 including brethren, instruction in singing to the Lord and each having understanding. The total is not limited only to the named immediate sons.
Retain lots for courses, small and great, accomplished and learners. The two paired descriptions remain rather than being reduced to age alone.

Retain the selected first-lot sequence Asaph, Joseph, Godolia and second Enia, with brethren before sons in the latter clause and twelve stated there. Do not move Godolia to the second lot or add a first-lot twelve.
column3: The initial grouping, the identity of Enia and the relation of Godolia to Joseph remain unresolved; the selected sequence is not an accepted reconstructed roster.

column2: Retain third Zakchour, sons and brethren, twelve. This order of sons before brethren differs from the preceding second-lot clause.
Retain fourth Jesdri and the twelve-member sons-and-brethren formula. Do not substitute Souri merely to match the earlier family list.
Retain fifth Nathanias with sons and brethren, twelve. The selected rank is fifth despite the earlier order of his family roster.
Retain sixth Boukias with sons and brethren, twelve. The total belongs to the stated group, not twelve sons plus additional brethren.
Retain seventh Iseriel with sons and brethren, twelve. Its relation to Erael in verse 2 is not silently resolved by respelling.
Retain eighth Josia with sons and brethren, twelve. Do not normalize Josia to Isaia from the prior list.
Retain ninth Manthanias with sons and brethren, twelve. The name remains distinct from fourteenth Mattathias.
Retain tenth Semei with sons and brethren, twelve. Semei is present both in the six-son roster and this lot list.
Retain eleventh Azaria with sons and brethren, twelve. Do not silently replace this selected form with Azarael from verse 4.
Retain twelfth Asabia with sons and brethren, twelve. Ordinal twelve and the group total twelve serve different functions.
Retain thirteenth Soubael with sons and brethren, twelve. The name matches this chapter's introductory roster without proving identity with another family's Soubael.
Retain fourteenth Mattathias with sons and brethren, twelve. The name is not merged with Manthanias in the ninth lot.
Retain fifteenth Jerimoth with sons and brethren, twelve. The lot order remains distinct from the introductory family order.
Retain sixteenth Ananias with sons and brethren, twelve. Ananias and eighteenth Anani remain separate selected entries.
Retain seventeenth Jesbakasa with sons and brethren, twelve. No duplicated family-count explanation is inserted.
Retain eighteenth Anani with sons and brethren, twelve. The shorter name is not expanded to Ananias.
Retain nineteenth Mellethi with sons and brethren, twelve. The selected spelling differs from Mallethi in verse 4 and remains provisional.
Retain twentieth Eliatha with sons and brethren, twelve. The inherited English represents the selected form without adding a title.
Retain twenty-first Ethir with sons and brethren, twelve. Its relation to Otheri in verse 4 remains an onomastic question, not a silent normalization.
Retain twenty-second Godollathi with sons and brethren, twelve. Godollathi is not merged with the differently spelled Godolia in earlier verses.
Retain twenty-third Meazoth with sons and brethren, twelve. The penultimate lot is preserved despite Meazoth ending the initial family list.
Retain twenty-fourth Romemthi-od with sons and brethren, twelve. The joined name and final rank remain; no new total is added to reconcile the unusual first lot.
